Maintenance Report — MNT-0018-007

Asset: WELL-0018 (SW-23 Well 018, T200, Southwest Block 23) Equipment: pump jack Work started: 14 Oct 2023 08:00 · Finished: 24 Oct 2023 11:00 · Well stopped for this job: 243 hours Crew lead: Megan Ward (U-305) · Crew: Brian Coleman · Contractor: Coyote Ridge Well Services Triggered by: inspection INS-0018-0052 on 2023-10-12 Report written: 24 Oct 2023

What happened

Field staff reported that oil was dripping from the gearbox onto the pump jack base. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0018-0052 showed the wellhead at 25.2 °C with the air at 21.1 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. The input shaft seal was worn and the gearbox oil level was below the sight glass. The well stayed shut in for about 8 days longer than the repair itself because the replacement part was back-ordered from the supplier.

Root cause

A hardened output shaft seal after years of service.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 1 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).

Work done

  1. Drained the gearbox oil into a closed container.
  2. Replaced the input and output shaft seals.
  3. Cleaned the base and absorbed the spilled oil.
  4. Refilled with the specified gear oil to the correct level.

Summary of the fix: replaced gearbox seals and topped up oil.

Testing and return to service

Ran the unit for 1 hour and checked both shafts for leaks: none found. The well was returned to production.

Waste

  • Used gear oil and oily pads sent to an approved disposal site under waste manifest WM-0018-007 (WS-06).

Maintenance Report — MNT-0018-009

Asset: WELL-0018 (SW-23 Well 018, T200, Southwest Block 23) Equipment: flowline Work started: 17 Nov 2023 08:00 · Finished: 17 Nov 2023 18:00 · Well stopped for this job: 10 hours Crew lead: Daniel Foster (U-302) · Crew: Brian Coleman Triggered by: inspection INS-0018-0057 on 2023-11-16 Report written: 18 Nov 2023

What happened

The weekly drone inspection INS-0018-0057 at 07:15 on 2023-11-16 found crude oil on the pad: about 11.2% of the pad area, estimated 3.4 bbl. The inspector noted: "Staining along flowline route." The field operator shut the well in, closed the flowline valve and placed earth berms and absorbent pads. The release was contained about 3.8 hours after the inspection. The crew traced the leak to a corrosion hole along the flowline route.

Root cause

External corrosion where the pipe coating had been damaged.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 0 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).
  • Hot work permit issued for welding; gas test before welding read 3% LEL, below the 10% limit (WS-04).

Work done

  1. Excavated around the leak point.
  2. Cut out the corroded section.
  3. Welded in new line pipe.
  4. Coated the new joints.
  5. Excavated the stained soil.
  6. Backfilled after the pressure test.

Summary of the fix: replaced leaking flowline section and remediated soil.

Testing and return to service

Pressure-tested the repaired section at 244 psi (1.25 × the flowline's maximum operating pressure of 195 psi) and held it for 4 hours with no pressure drop (WS-05). The well was returned to production.

Spill clean-up and waste

  • About 3.9 m³ of stained soil excavated, bagged and sent to an approved disposal site under waste manifest WM-0018-009 (WS-06).
  • 2 soil samples taken around the spill; the highest result after clean-up was 0.59% TPH, below the 1.0% target (SR-03).

Maintenance Report — MNT-0018-013

Asset: WELL-0018 (SW-23 Well 018, T200, Southwest Block 23) Equipment: pump jack Work started: 26 May 2024 08:00 · Finished: 19 Jun 2024 07:00 · Well stopped for this job: 575 hours Crew lead: Brian Coleman (U-304) · Crew: Megan Ward · Contractor: Coyote Ridge Well Services Triggered by: inspection INS-0018-0083 on 2024-05-23 Report written: 19 Jun 2024

What happened

Field staff reported that the pumper heard grinding from the walking beam and saw the horsehead wobbling. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0018-0083 showed the wellhead at 37.2 °C with the air at 34.3 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. A vibration check and visual inspection found play in the saddle bearing and scoring on the bearing housing. The well stayed shut in for about 22 days longer than the repair itself because the replacement part was back-ordered from the supplier.

Root cause

Grease contaminated with sand had worn the bearing.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 2 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).

Work done

  1. Lowered the horsehead and supported the walking beam with a crane.
  2. Removed the saddle bearing assembly.
  3. Cleaned the housing and checked alignment.
  4. Fitted a new saddle bearing and torqued the bolts to the manufacturer's values.
  5. Greased all structural bearings.

Summary of the fix: replaced saddle bearing and re-greased.

Testing and return to service

Ran the unit for 2 hours: smooth stroke, no knocking, bearing temperature normal. The well was returned to production.

Notes and recommendations

  • Shorten the grease interval on this unit to 60 days.
  • Check saddle bearings on neighbouring units of the same age.
